messages:
derek.h: Observing sporadic 95th/99th percentile tail spikes on continuous-batching with long (>=64k) contexts. Looks correlated with KV cache "hot" hits and large batch coalescing windows. Repro on stage: warm cache, high QPS, many long prefix requests.

amy: Can you paste the minimal repro and a perf snapshot? Is this new after the merge that changed merge/split heuristics?

derek.h: Repro steps: run continuous-batcher with --max-batch=64 --coalesce-ms=12, feed long-context chat sessions (20–40k tokens) mixed with short requests. After ~10m you see a lat spike and a node with high resident memory. Attached pprof excerpt below.

chris: quick note from the flame: the hot path is dominated by "kv_fetch_pages" (blocking) with many goroutines stuck waiting on page-level locks while one goroutine performs an evict/compact. Head-of-line effect because batch coalescer groups requests that all need KV pages; when one request triggers eviction, the whole merged batch stalls.

chris: snippet from pprof (stack simplified):
```
kv_fetch_pages
  kv_store.go:412 (rw lock)
  kvcache_pager.go:237 (evictAndCompact)
  batch_coalesce.go:89 (mergeAndDispatch)
  continuous_batcher.go:141
```

sree: Also saw memory climb in long-tail tests. The pager's compaction does a temporary allocation equal to ~1.2x working set while rebuilding index; combined with continuous batching holding references to KV nodes prevents GC which amplifies memory growth.

amy: So root cause hypothesis: coalescing merges many requests that simultaneously touch overlapping KV pages; if one request path triggers a synchronous eviction/compaction the merged payload is blocked -> HOL (head-of-line) for all requests in that merged batch. That both increases latency and prolongs references preventing GC.

derek.h: Exactly. Two quick mitigations we tried locally: 1) reduce coalesce-ms from 12 to 2 (reduces merge size), 2) make evict/compact asynchronous (spawn background compaction and return with a soft-failure so other batch members can proceed with fallback). Both reduced spikes but had tradeoffs: (1) increases per-token overhead at low QPS, (2) async compaction risks transient higher memory.

chris: We also profiled a variant where "kv_fetch_pages" used sharded page locks rather than a global page mutex. Reduced hol stall time by ~6x in the microbench but required careful correctness checks for concurrent evict+read.

amy: Can you share numbers? Q95/Q99 before/after?

chris: Perf numbers from stage run (peak load):
- baseline (coalesce=12, sync-compact): p95=120ms p99=860ms mem-rss=28GB
- coalesce=2: p95=95ms p99=420ms mem-rss=30GB
- async-compact (coalesce=12): p95=110ms p99=350ms mem-rss=34GB
- sharded-locks + coalesce=8: p95=88ms p99=210ms mem-rss=29GB

sree: Notably async-compact + coalesce kept latency reasonable but RAM rose due to delayed reclaim. The sharded-lock approach looks promising but needs code review for race conditions.

amy: OK action items: (A) short-term: lower default coalesce-ms to 4 for long-context workloads and expose knob in console per-model. (B) medium-term: implement sharded page locks + add metrics for "batch_coalesced_size" and "kv-evict-duration". (C) investigation: safe async compaction variant that caps extra memory and yields to other readers.

chris: I'll prototype sharded locks PR and add microbench. Derek/ Sree, can you validate async-compact with forced OOM tests and confirm fallback correctness?

sree: I'll run the OOM and long-run memtests (24h) on the PR pipeline. Also will add a check to the pager: if compaction would allocate >20% extra working set, abort and revert to a conservative eviction that pages out small chunks to avoid massive temporary alloc.

derek.h: I'll update the continuous-batcher tests to fuzz coalesce timing and merge sizes, add a test that simulates a compaction stall to assert downstream requests see graceful fallback rather than full batch stall.

infra-bot: deploy:staging started by chris at 1847654120 — rolling out addl logging for kvpager/compaction-duration.

amy: Great. One more thing: can we add a console alert for sudden increase in "batch_coalesced_size" or sustained "kv-evict-duration>200ms" to auto-toggle coalesce-ms on overloaded nodes?

chris: Yes, I'll wire CUE alert -> autoset (soft throttle) prototype.

amy: Thanks team, let's sync tomorrow after the microbench PR and the 24h memtest results. :thumbsup:
